Day 11 of 100 · AWS Networking Foundations

VPC Endpoints

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityAWS Networking FoundationsTopic verified by artifact

VPC Endpoints let workloads reach supported AWS services without making the public internet the required data path.

Architecture / mental model

Private workload → VPC endpoint → supported AWS service

How it works

Interface endpoints use AWS PrivateLink and place endpoint network interfaces in selected subnets. Gateway endpoints provide route-table targets for supported services such as Amazon S3 and DynamoDB.

The security benefit is architectural: a private workload can reach a service through an AWS-managed private path instead of depending on an Internet Gateway or NAT path just to call an AWS API.

Endpoint policies, Security Groups on interface endpoints, route tables and DNS all influence whether the path works. Creating an endpoint is only one part of the connection.

Hands-on reference

aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints
aws ec2 describe-route-tables

Verification

Resolve the service name from the workload, inspect endpoint state and route/DNS behavior, then prove the request succeeds without the public egress path the endpoint was meant to replace.

Field note / gotcha

Private DNS on an interface endpoint can change where a familiar public service hostname resolves inside the VPC. DNS is part of endpoint design, not an afterthought.

Security considerations

Scope endpoint policies and attached Security Groups. A private path is useful, but private does not automatically mean least privilege.

What I learned

Network design improves when private workloads do not need unnecessary public egress just to use cloud-native services.
